question.text: Patanjali Herbals Fund (Cat II): INR 120 crore committed and called. Hurdle 9% compounded. Fund tenure 4 years. Compute the cumulative PREFERRED RETURN at end of Year 4 (return accruing solely to investors before any GP carry).

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Hurdle NAV Year 4 = INR 120 x (1.09)^4 = INR 120 x 1.41158 = INR 169.39 crore. Preferred return = 169.39 - 120 = INR 49.39 crore (≈ INR 49.38 cr). **The Trap:** A is simple interest 9% x 4 x 120 = INR 43.20 cr (wrong — compound not simple); C is 5-year compound; D is 9% x 2 yr. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests same. Compound preferred return is Chapter 6's standard. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Show LPs the full preferred-return schedule in year-end reports — not just the cumulative. This transparency builds trust and is painless to produce if you've modelled compound correctly from Day 1.
